Following Event evaluation does not enforce the security of related notes or groups, so sensitive events should be secured consistently with the records they represent.

The default Sign-Up registration and reminder communications use SMS as well as email; an organization phone number must be configured on those system communications to prevent errors when they are sent.

A Sign-Up Overview communication sends each selected recipient only one message even when that person is registered for multiple selected opportunities; the Opportunities Lava collection can be iterated to include details for each registration.
The questions and available answer formats in Rock's built-in assessments cannot be configured.

To use a custom group type for Sign-Ups, inherit it from the Sign-Up Group type, allow it as a child of the original type, configure at least one group schedule option and location selection mode, and include it in the Sign-Up Finder block's Project Types setting.

An Interactive Experience can associate interactions with a campus using schedule filtering by nearby campus geofences, the person's current geofence, or the campus stored on the person's record; either geofence-based mode requires geofences configured for the campuses.

The occurrence map defines which eligible days or weeks count as possible meetings for a streak type; changes to the map are not reflected in participants' displayed streak data until the nightly cleanup job runs.

A step program's completion flow controls ordering and prerequisites: Linear (Required) enforces sequence and removes custom prerequisites, Linear (Preferred) allows out-of-order completion while enforcing prerequisites, and Non-Linear uses ordering only for display while enforcing prerequisites.
An achievement attempt closes when it succeeds or fails; if Allow Overachievement is enabled, its displayed progress can exceed 100 percent.
The Spiritual Gifts Assessment classifies a person's results as dominant, supportive, and other gifts, and those result attributes can be queried with person Data Views.
Rebuilding an achievement type deletes and recalculates each person's attempt data occurring after that person's latest successful attempt.
The Experience Manager supports approving or rejecting moderated responses; its campus-filterable Live Questions view excludes responses that require approval until they have been approved.

When Rock rebuilds an attendance-based streak type, it derives the streak start date, enrolled people, individual enrollment dates, engagement counts and applicable occurrence weeks from attendance data; weeks recorded as "Didn’t Meet" are excluded from the occurrence map and do not count as attendance gaps.
For a Rhythm engagement type, Rock does not automatically change a person's step status; In Progress represents an active rhythm, while Completed indicates that the rhythm has ended.
A following suggestion must be active to run; its Reminded Days value controls how long Rock waits before presenting an unfollowed suggestion again, while a blank value prevents reminders.

Transferring a Step Type between programs does not recalculate or relocate existing Program Completions; historical completions remain associated with the programs in which they were originally recorded.
When Add Step on Success is enabled for an achievement type, successfully completing the achievement can add a step to the configured step program and step type with the selected status.

A repeating reminder schedules its next occurrence from the date the current occurrence is completed, rather than from its original due date; leaving the repeat-count field empty makes the recurrence indefinite.
Rock simplifies DISC reporting to four levels on each DISC scale and maps the results to 16 single-letter or two-letter personality types for use in group and team contexts.
A Step Program Trends chart includes only completed step types, while a Step Type chart can show activity for either started or completed steps.
The History tab on a person's profile lists both requested and self-initiated assessments; self-initiated entries have no request date or requester.
An achievement type defines a goal that Rock can automatically evaluate from engagement or interaction data while tracking each entity's progress toward completion.
Creating a sign-up group requires Edit permission for the Project Type group attribute; creating one at the top level additionally requires Edit permission on the Sign-Up Groups block.
For more consistent assessment results, respondents should answer according to their present characteristics and use the same environmental context throughout the assessment.

The built-in In Group Together and In Followed Group suggestion types can restrict eligible followers and suggested people by group type, group, group role, or security role, depending on the configured limiter.
Data views can filter people by results from any assessment available in Rock, enabling organizations to group those people and report on their assessment responses.

Outreach Toolbox can track contact-specific prayer and connection cadences, completed touchpoint history and periodic pulse updates, with configurable milestone prompts. Review who can see the contact data and which block settings are enabled before ministry use.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: A user can follow someone from that person's profile, add or remove multiple followed people through bulk updates, and manage the resulting list under My Settings > Following.

The Motivators assessment results include a growth-propensity measure, a composite score, ranked motivators, and the person's leading motivator themes, with detailed descriptions focused on the highest scores.
A streak type defines the engagement source, time pattern and start date Rock uses to calculate streaks, as well as the population enrolled for tracking.

A step generated from an achievement uses the achievement completion date as its configured start or end date, respects step prerequisites, and is created repeatedly for recurring achievements only when the step type permits multiple completions.

On a step type's participant list, the start-date column is shown only when the step type spans time; for a step type that does not span time, its single step date is displayed as the completion date.
Moving a Step Type to another Step Program preserves its step data but removes its prerequisites and Step Attributes, which must be configured again after the transfer.
Step chart status filters determine which event date is plotted: completed statuses use each step's completion date, while other statuses use its start date.

A reminder can be added manually only when the current page provides context for the target entity and a reminder type exists for that entity type; reminders can also be created automatically with a workflow action.
In Rock 19.0, Content Collections depend on Universal Search and require an active Universal Search index component.
The Tools > Content screen can limit the channel list to channels with pending items, while a selected channel's items can be filtered by status, date range, or title.
A church can selectively publish content to the Content Library, where it is stored in a Spark-hosted cloud environment and can be downloaded into another church's Rock instance.
In Rock 19.0, the Asset Manager under Admin Tools > CMS Configuration manages files and folders in configured storage providers, including cloud storage and the Rock server.
Avoid output caching on a Content Channel View block when its rendered content is personalized, because cached output can expose one visitor's personalized values to another visitor.
Rock can personalize website content for visitors who are not logged in by using available browsing-session and visitor signals.

The Content Channel Item Self Update job evaluates Lava stored in a content channel item attribute and writes the result to another item attribute; the Lava output must be compatible with the target attribute's field type.
After configuring a page's Open Graph metadata, use Facebook's Share Validator to preview the resulting share and inspect debugging information.
With view tracking enabled on the adaptivemessage Lava command, an adaptation stops displaying to a viewer after its configured saturation count is reached within the configured day range.
Rock includes a File Manager block under Admin Tools > CMS Configuration > File Manager that supports uploading and deleting files and managing directories.

Request Filters can personalize content without identifying the visitor by evaluating request context such as site, new-or-returning status, device type, query parameters, cookies, browser version, IP range, IP-derived location, and visit day or time.

In Rock, the Organization Currency Code controls the currency symbol shown with numeric amounts but does not convert values or configure payment processing; payment gateways must use the matching currency to avoid incorrect account crediting.
To enable international address entry and display, set the Support International Addresses global attribute to Yes under Admin Tools > Settings > Global Attributes.
Changing a localization display setting does not necessarily change the underlying processing behavior; for example, selecting a different currency symbol does not reconfigure the payment gateway.
To use personalization on a Rock site, enable the site's Enable Personalization setting under Admin Tools > Websites.
Content Library functionality is enabled per Content Channel and applies to every item in that channel; uploading an individual item to the library requires both an Experience Level and a Topic.
Public calendar event templates can use social metadata through Lava, and event attributes provide separately formatted images for Facebook and Twitter sharing.

For a Rock Media element with multiple generated files, such as HLS, HD, or SD variants, the desired file's URL can be copied from the element's Media Files page and used as the Media Player shortcode source.
Changing a Content Channel's Content Library license affects only later uploads; items already uploaded retain the license assigned when they were uploaded.

A required Media Watch attribute can prevent submission of a workflow form until the participant has watched the configured percentage of its single assigned video; progress counts unique watched seconds, so seeking ahead does not satisfy the requirement.

Universal Channel Types provide attribute-free starting points for one-off content channels, allowing each channel to define all of its required item attributes without creating a dedicated channel type.

Content Channel Types define the attributes available on channels and their content items; Content Channels instantiate those types for a particular publishing purpose, and Content Items hold the individual entries within each channel.

To render a Content Channel Item's Media Element with watch interactions and analytics, read the raw value of a Media Element item attribute and pass its GUID to the Media Player shortcode's media parameter rather than using src.
Content Component output caching can improve page speed, but it should be avoided for personalized output because a cached response can expose content intended for a different visitor.

Rock's dynamic content model uses content channel types to define available channel and item attributes, content channels to instantiate those types for a particular purpose, and content items to store the individual entries within each channel.
Set a page description in Page Settings for pages likely to be shared on social media; otherwise, social platforms may derive the share description from page content instead.
When displaying a numeric currency value in Lava, use the FormatAsCurrency filter to apply the symbol associated with the configured Organization Currency Code.
Enable Visitor Tracking in the site settings when the site's personalization should use visitor activity data.
A content channel item can use items from other channels as children; each child can belong to multiple parents and can have child items of its own.

Podcast series graphics use the Unsecured file type by default, which stores them in the database; configure a file type backed by the file system or an external storage provider to avoid consuming database space.
When a viewer qualifies for multiple Adaptive Message adaptations, their configured order determines which message is selected.
A person must satisfy every configured filter area in a personalization segment, while conditions within an individual area can use either Any or All matching logic.
The Library Viewer must be opened from a Content Channel's Download from Library action so Rock knows which channel should receive the downloaded content.
A Content Channel Item is displayed no earlier than its Start date and can be automatically removed from display by assigning an Expire date.
When Content Collection changes are not reflected during the day, manually running the Index Content Collections system job can refresh the collection before its automatic overnight run.
Rock can automatically create a Content Channel Item for a video uploaded to a video service provider, allowing the video to be published and its engagement tracked within Rock.

Using website personalization requires configuring Personalization Segments for person data or browsing behavior, Request Filters for session characteristics such as device or IP address, and the relevant site settings.
Rock ranks trending content collection items by dividing each item's interactions during the configured Trending Window by the item's age in days, with the age divisor capped at the window length.
To use a Media Watch attribute on a workflow entry form, configure it as both visible and editable; auto-resume is disabled when its lookback period is blank or zero days.
In Rock 19.0, a content component template's Display Lava can use both the component's related content channel items and its configuration settings.
Content collections do not enforce the individual security settings of indexed items, so displaying a collection can expose restricted content to people who could not access it elsewhere in Rock.
Rock's basic podcast implementation uses the Podcast Series and Podcast Messages content channels, which can be extended with additional attributes.
Channel attributes store information shared by a channel, while item attributes store additional structured values separately for each content item.

The Media Player shortcode defaults autoresumeindays and combineplaystatisticsindays to 7 days; setting both to 14 means a viewer returning after more than 14 days starts from the beginning and the watch is recorded as a new Individual Play.

A channel feed uses the default RSS Lava template unless TemplateId selects another Lava Templates defined value; Count limits returned items and defaults to 10, while EnableDebug exposes the template's available merge fields.

Personalization segment membership is stored in PersonAliasPersonalization, where PersonAliasId identifies the person alias, PersonalizationType is 0 for segment records, and PersonalizationEntityId identifies the matched segment.
Adaptive Messages centralize multiple message adaptations behind one Lava command and can select variants using personalization data, date windows, view counts, and optional saturation limits.
When a content channel uses approvals, only users with Approval permission can set a content item's approval status.
Under Tools > Content, staff can access channels for which they have View permission, see each channel's pending-item count, and open a channel to manage its content items.
The Update Personalization Data job reevaluates personalization segment conditions and adds or removes people from each segment's current membership list accordingly.

Rock Media can preserve a person's playback progress when they move between mobile and web, and the Media Player shortcode configuration controls whether those viewing sessions appear in analytics as one combined watch or separate watches.
Leaving a Content Component item attribute's Categories field empty makes that attribute available to every Content Component template.
To let a security role approve Content Channel Items, grant the role the Approve permission on the Rock.Model.ContentChannelType entity through Entity Administration.

A Media Element analytics page reports aggregate engagement, rewatches, play counts, cumulative viewing time, and daily plays, while individual play records can show the viewer, viewing time, portions watched or repeated, device category, ISP, operating system, and browser.

Configure a separate Content Channel Item Self Update job for each content channel, setting Template Key to the item attribute that contains the Lava and Target Key to the item attribute the evaluated result should update.

Rock stores a person's matching personalization segments in the ROCK_SEGMENT_FILTERS browser cookie and refreshes it every five minutes by default; administrators can change that interval with the Personalization Segment Cookie Affinity Duration system setting.
To control a page's Facebook share preview, use Lava's AddMetaTagToHead filter in an HTML block to add Open Graph title, description, and image metadata.
GetImage.ashx can resize an image from its file GUID using width and height query parameters; its max, pad, stretch, and crop options determine how the image fits the requested dimensions.
When troubleshooting dates or times displayed in a US format, first inspect the server culture shown in the System Information dialog, which is available from the Admin Toolbar.
A content item's available date fields are determined by its content channel type, which can configure items for a single date, a date range, or no dates.

The Asset field type can be used as an attribute on entities such as content channels, people, and groups, allowing editors to choose files or images stored through an integrated remote cloud storage provider such as Azure or Amazon S3.
Use an Asset attribute or the HTML editor's asset picker when editors need explicit control over file storage or need to reuse files already present in a configured cloud provider.

The Lava Personalize command conditionally renders content when the current person or request matches the segment key or request-filter key supplied to the command, and it can be used in both page content and communications.

To scope a Content Component item attribute to particular templates, create a Content Channel Item attribute category whose name exactly matches each target template, then assign the attribute to the applicable category or categories.
A content component lets a designer define markup and Lava behavior while giving editors structured values to change, reducing the need for editors to modify fragile HTML directly.

Rock initially associates an anonymous visitor's tracked page views with a Person Alias record, then links that alias to the identified Person record when the visitor logs in so the prior activity is attributed to that person.

Rock localization is configured through independent settings for areas such as phone numbers, regional date and time display, currency symbols, addresses, and school grades; organizations can adjust only the areas they need.
A content collection's Trending Gravity setting adjusts trending scores to favor newer items relative to older items.
To execute Lava stored in a Content Channel Item's Content field on a Content Channel Item View block, configure the block's Lava Template to process Item.Content with the RunLava filter.
Set the twitter:card metadata to summary_large_image for a large-image share card or summary for a small-image share card.
Rock can automatically create a Content Channel Item when a media element is added to a folder, provided the target Content Channel has a Media Element item attribute for storing the video.
The GetChannelFeed.ashx endpoint publishes items from the content channel identified by the required ChannelId query parameter, provided that RSS is enabled for that channel.
A Content Component block can restrict displayed content using one or more Content Channel Item fields or attributes as filters.
Each external media source requires its own Media Account and a provider plugin, while Rock's built-in Local Media Account requires folders, media elements, and metadata to be maintained manually.

In Lava, use AddMetaTagToHead to set the twitter:title, twitter:description, and twitter:image metadata that controls a page's Twitter/X share presentation; the image value must be a URL for an image uploaded to the website.

Configure each supported country with its abbreviation, localized City, State, and Postal Code labels, and display format; for commonly used countries, add Address States linked to the country with both an abbreviation in Value and a full name in Description.
Personalization features for content channel items must be enabled in the configuration of their content channel.

For a personalized Content Channel Item, matching any configured segment and any configured request filter is sufficient within each group, but an item that uses both groups requires a match in both groups.

To support phone formats for additional countries, add entries under Admin Tools > Settings > Defined Types > Phone Country Code with the dialing code, a description, a regular expression that matches the entered number, and a formatting expression that maps captured number groups to placeholders.

When multiple phone countries are configured, phone inputs include a country-code selector and default to the first entry in the Phone Country Code defined type; administrators can reorder those entries to change the default.
Content Channel Items have an Interact permission that can let everyone see that an item exists while restricting access to its full content to people with that permission.

For personalization logic that requires explicit conditional handling, the Lava PersonalizationItems filter can determine whether the current person belongs to a specified personalization segment or matches a request filter.

Personalization segments require persisted data views, so their membership is not updated in real time; after refreshing an underlying data view, run the Update Personalization Data job to bring the segment's person list up to date.

Anonymous visitor personalization requires Enable Visitor Tracking on each applicable site; Rock uses a browser cookie to recognize returning visitors, with a default persistence of 365 days that can be changed using Visitor Cookie Persistence Length in System Configuration.
A Content Collection can combine any number of content channels and calendars so their content can be searched together from one collection.

A Request Filter's key should omit spaces and special characters because it is used to reference the filter from Lava's PersonalizationItems filter or Personalize command; leaving the Site setting blank allows the Request Filter to apply across all sites.
The Media Player Lava shortcode can embed a video by passing its URL in the shortcode's src parameter; supported sources include YouTube URLs and URLs for files managed through Rock Media.

A content collection can evaluate personalization segments, request filters, or both; the Content Collection View block can then be configured to rank matching content channel items higher in its results.
Social-sharing metadata can be customized by placing the network-specific meta tags, generated with Lava when needed, in an HTML block on the page.
When personalization is configured on the Content Collection View block, content channel items matching the current person or visit are promoted in search results by the configured boost amount.

When an external CDN or image optimization service should perform image resizing, add disableoptimizations=true to the GetImage.ashx query to prevent Rock and the external service from both resizing or optimizing the image.

In Rock 19.0, administrators can create content component templates under Admin Tools > CMS Configuration > Content Component Templates and can inspect the Lava context by placing the Lava Debug expression in the Display Lava field.
When adding a child to a content channel item, an editor can either link an existing content item or create a new one during the same workflow.

When content items contain Lava that depends on the current person or other contextual merge values, provide fallback behavior because those values may be unavailable when the same content is rendered through the channel's RSS feed.

Enabling content-channel synchronization on a Media Folder creates a Content Channel Item for each newly added media element; the selected channel must have a Media Element item attribute to store the associated media.
If externally uploaded files do not appear in an Asset Manager folder in Rock 19.0, refresh that folder to update its displayed file list.
A personalization segment's Person Filter requires a persisted data view, so its membership is not evaluated in real time and cannot include anonymous visitors.
The available Universal Channel Types differ only in which date fields they expose, including an option for channels that do not use dates.
Configure a File Manager block's root folder and permissions to let a user or security role manage only a designated portion of the file hierarchy without providing FTP credentials.
A content channel type defines whether its items use a single date, a date range, or no date, and can remove priority, content, or approval-status fields when those concepts do not apply.

Content downloaded through a Content Channel's Library Viewer is created as a new item in that channel; downloading it again refreshes the existing item and overwrites any local changes made since the prior download.
Public field-type configuration keys and their meanings form a compatibility contract with remote consumers such as Rock Mobile, so changing them can break existing clients.

An Obsidian grid CopyColumn renders a button that copies text to the browser clipboard; it uses the row value identified by the column's field setting unless valueToCopy is supplied to compute the text from the row, column definition, and grid state.
BooleanColumn uses defaults for the standard formatComponent and exportValue properties and does not introduce any column-specific properties.
In an Obsidian grid, SelectColumn renders row-selection checkboxes that allow grid actions to operate on multiple selected rows.

An Obsidian block requires a C# server component for its logic, while its client component supplies the user interface and may be omitted for a web block that only returns static HTML without interactions.

In an Obsidian grid, DateColumn renders the value of its configured field as a short-form date and supplies defaults for formatting, skeleton display, quick-filter values, and exported values; it adds no column-specific properties.
The Obsidian Browser Bus is a page-local publish-subscribe mechanism backed by DOM events; its messages do not cross browser tabs or reach another user's browser.

When an Obsidian field type uses different public display and edit representations, its client-side value-formatting methods must accept either representation because an unsaved edit component value can be supplied where the display representation is normally expected.

For an Obsidian plugin, `npm run build` performs TypeScript type checking before compiling and copying assets to RockWeb, whereas `npm run watch` continuously recompiles changed files without type checking.
Obsidian block actions are stateless server calls, so every action must revalidate client data and recheck authorization rather than relying on TypeScript visibility or a previous C# instance.

Generated detail-block save handlers initially treat every selected property as writable, so properties included only to control the UI, such as IsSystem, must be removed from the saveable-property list to prevent unintended database updates.
Set an Obsidian Grid's key field to the data property that uniquely identifies each row when using advanced grid features that depend on row identity.
Obsidian block clients exchange JSON data with their C# server component and invoke block actions through endpoints that retain the block's settings and normal security enforcement.
An Obsidian grid LabelColumn can translate raw field values into display text with textSource, then use that translated text as the lookup key for classSource or colorSource styling.

A Universal Field Type keeps UI code outside its C# field-type implementation and supplies structured data for the client framework to render; item, tree, and search picker implementations using this pattern also receive Data View filtering support.

When NumberBadgeColumn ranges overlap, the effective precedence from highest to lowest is danger, warning, success, info, then hidden; therefore a matching color range can override a configured hide range.
The Obsidian grid SecurityColumn displays a per-row control that opens Rock's standard security editor for the corresponding item.
Attaching the VS Code debugger to an existing Chrome session requires Chrome to be launched with remote debugging enabled on port 9222.
Obsidian's NumberBadgeColumn displays a number in a badge and selects its color by testing the value against configured inclusive minimum and maximum ranges.
PersonColumn can link a displayed person to the person detail page, but it does not verify that the viewer is authorized to access that page; the documented showAsLink behavior is scoped to Rock 17.

After ReorderColumn updates the grid's row order, its optional onOrderChanged callback receives the moved row and the row now following it, or null when moved to the end; the callback can persist the change, return false to cancel it, or return a promise that blocks further reordering until completion.

Every Obsidian detail block should enforce either entity security, which authorizes against the displayed entity, or CMS security, which uses the block's permissions; when replacing an unsecured WebForms detail block, start with CMS security and review the effective page permissions.
In an Obsidian grid, a generic Column can display custom cell content by defining the format template and using its row value to render the desired markup.
AttributeColumns does not support the standard grid column properties, but it can be configured with an attribute filter and a skeleton component shown while grid data is loading.

An Obsidian field type must convert private field and configuration data into transmission-safe public representations; identifiers may also be expanded into client-friendly objects when the client needs additional display data, with a corresponding conversion back to the stored representation.
The Rock VS Code workspace provides separate debugger configurations for the Obsidian Framework and Obsidian Blocks projects, with options to launch a new browser or attach to an existing one.

In a rock-dev-tool setup, the development environment owns the runnable Rock installation and selected Rock version, while each plugin remains a separate source repository that can be attached to multiple environments for testing against different Rock versions.
Values whose changes must update an Obsidian component's template should use reactive ref or computed values; changing an ordinary variable does not notify the template to render again.

The Obsidian grid EditColumn invokes its optional click callback with the row key; the callback may be synchronous or return a Promise, in which case the edit button stays disabled until that Promise settles.

An Obsidian grid ButtonColumn renders one icon button and requires both an icon CSS class and a click handler; the handler receives the row key and current grid state and may complete synchronously or asynchronously.
SecurityColumn uses the row's "isSecurityDisabled" field by default to disable its security control when that field is true; a different row field can be selected through disabledField.
RockFieldColumn requires an attribute definition, which it uses to format the field value for display.
An Obsidian grid custom column filter combines a popup component that constructs the filter value with a predicate function that receives each row and that value to decide whether the row matches.

An Obsidian block can grant child controls scoped API access by creating a server-side security grant, sending its token in block configuration, providing that grant in the client component tree, and including the injected token in control API requests; the block should expose token renewal because these tokens expire after one hour by default.
The Obsidian grid DateTimeColumn formats a cell as a short date and time, showing the date, hour, and minutes by default; setting showSeconds to true adds seconds.

In an Obsidian grid, HighlightDetailColumn renders its primary field in bold and can render a secondary row-property value beneath it when detailField names that property; omitting detailField or setting it to false leaves the secondary area empty.

For most Obsidian pickers, `showBlankItem` controls whether a selected value can be cleared, while the `required` validation rule independently controls whether the form can be submitted without a value.
In an Obsidian grid, BooleanColumn renders a checkmark when its bound value is true and leaves the cell empty otherwise.
Obsidian developer documentation may describe core-only patterns; plugin developers should apply a documented pattern only after determining that it also applies to plugins.

Plugin endpoints that supply Universal Tree Item Picker or Search Picker data should accept POST input from the request body and use an `api/v2/plugins/{organization-code}/...` route; the `api/v2` prefix produces the camel-cased response properties expected by Obsidian clients, while the organization segment avoids plugin route collisions.

Obsidian's `cachePromise` utility wraps a Promise-returning operation so concurrent calls with the same wrapper reuse the in-flight Promise, and later calls reuse the serialized result until its expiration time; the default expiration is one minute.
DeleteColumn can disable deletion per row through rowDisabled, and when its onClick callback returns a Promise, the delete button stays disabled until that Promise resolves.
For core Obsidian development, the Code Generator can scaffold a basic list block that can then be customized; this generator is not available for plugin blocks.

Obsidian grids provide standard column filters for boolean, date, numeric, and text values, plus a filter that lets a person select one or more values from the column's unique existing values; the text filter uses substring matching.

In an Obsidian TypeScript model for JSON data, declare a property as optional when the server may omit it, and include `null` in its type when the server may also send an explicit null value; for example, a nullable string that may be omitted should use `property?: string | null`.
The Obsidian developer documentation is a work in progress, so described behavior may change or may not yet be implemented as documented.

In an Obsidian grid column, the format, condensed, header, and skeleton templates take precedence over their corresponding rendering component properties; condensedComponent falls back to formatComponent when no condensed component is specified.
Obsidian TypeScript code should import across packages with aliases such as `@Obsidian/...`; relative imports are reserved for files in the same package or directory.

Obsidian grids perform filtering, sorting, and paging in the browser, so the complete row set must be transferred before rendering; configuring a smaller page size does not reduce the amount of data sent to the client.

In an Obsidian grid, the AttributeColumns placeholder determines where dynamically generated columns for entity attribute values are inserted; its attributes property accepts the attribute definitions to display.

A Person grid that does not inherit from RockListBlockType must provide block actions for creating entity sets and communications, and its grid definition must identify a Person key field using an IdKey or GUID, for the corresponding default grid actions to work.
An Obsidian Grid can receive its required data directly or through a function; if that function returns a promise, the grid waits asynchronously for the result.
Obsidian's ReorderColumn renders a drag handle that lets a user move a row to a different position in the grid.
In an Obsidian grid, CurrencyColumn formats the cell value as currency and supplies default formatting, loading-skeleton, and export-value behavior without adding column-specific properties.
An Obsidian grid using PersonColumn must add its person field through AddPersonField() so the column receives all values required to render the person.

Core Obsidian additions must respect the package dependency hierarchy: a package may depend on packages above it in the hierarchy, but dependencies must not create direct or indirect cycles; block developers may import from any of the documented Obsidian packages.

In older Obsidian `.ts` files, a Vue compiler error reported only as `SyntaxError 15` indicates that whitespace is missing between attributes; this numeric-error troubleshooting issue is not expected for newer `.obs` files.

To make a core field type available in Obsidian, declare Obsidian platform support on its C# field type, expose its GUID through the generated field-type system GUIDs, and import and register its TypeScript implementation in the Obsidian field-type index.

To cache an Obsidian API request, import the cache utility from `@Obsidian/Utility/cache`, call `cachePromise` with a unique cache key, a function that returns the request Promise, and optionally an expiration time, then invoke the returned function instead of issuing the request directly.

A control API endpoint that accepts a security-grant token must reconstruct and evaluate the grant alongside the current person's normal authorization; unauthorized single-entity operations should return an unauthorized response, while list operations should omit entities the caller cannot access, using the authorization action appropriate to the operation.
In an Obsidian grid, TextColumn renders the field value as plain text and introduces no properties beyond the standard column properties.

An Obsidian block can provide a custom configuration screen by implementing `IHasCustomActions`, returning an administrate-only action whose component URL points to a separate `.obs` template, and exposing block actions to load and save the custom settings.
In an Obsidian component, a property's default is used only when the parent omits that property; explicitly passing null preserves null instead of substituting the default.

An Obsidian RockForm can be submitted by binding its submit prop and setting the bound value to true; after validation completes, the form resets that value to false and emits the submit event only when submission may proceed.
A JavaScript truthiness check rejects `undefined`, `null`, and an empty string together; use explicit comparisons instead when an Obsidian component must distinguish among those states.
The Obsidian grid DeleteColumn asks for confirmation before invoking its click handler by default; setting disableConfirmation to true bypasses that prompt.

Core `.obs` development is supported in Visual Studio Code rather than the Visual Studio editor, and the repository workspace supplies the expected settings and watch tasks for Obsidian controls and blocks.

Add an EditColumn to an Obsidian grid and assign its click handler to provide a per-row edit action; the column supplies defaults for its name, formatter component, header and item classes, and width.
LabelColumn styling can be configured either with classSource values that identify standard label suffixes or with colorSource values that specify CSS background colors.

In an Obsidian RockForm, input components report rule-validation results through their internal RockFormField; when the nearest form is submitted, RockForm blocks submission and displays its standard validation notice if any field is invalid, otherwise it emits the submit event.
The Obsidian grid NumberColumn formats numeric cell values using the browser's current locale, including its thousands and decimal separators.
RockFieldColumn is an internal Rock grid column for displaying one Rock field value and should not be used by plugins.
An Obsidian grid column can remain available to exports or other processing while hidden on screen with hideOnScreen, whereas excludeFromExport removes the column from export output.

An Obsidian field configuration change handled entirely in the client should emit an updated model value, while a change that requires refreshed server-derived options should additionally request a configuration update.

When multiple v19 registrant-eligibility rules are enabled, a registrant must satisfy all selected criteria. Test combined age, gender, grade and Data View rules with representative people before opening registration.
